subject: guinea_pig
readings: Head at +z: ZY panel is the profile (nose-to-tail along z, ~24 units), XY panel is the front (face-on) view, XZ is the top-down view

ZY panel: ear/head tuft near (z=17,y=5); rump edge near (z=3,y=6); body-center reference ~(z=12,y=12) -- head lies forward(+z) and slightly up(frame +y) from center, rump lies backward(-z) and slightly up as well (arched back)
ZY panel: front foot nub at (z=18,y=22) -- descends sharply from chest area, confirming short legs

XY panel: left cheek edge (x=3,y=9), right cheek edge (x=21,y=9), top of head (x=12,y=2), left front foot (x=7,y=23), right front foot (x=17,y=23) -- gives lateral leg spread of about ±5 units from midline
XZ panel: ear fur at screen-top (small z reading, ~2-4) confirms head is at high frame-z (forward), consistent with ZY reading; body oval spans x=2-22, z=4-24 matching torso width/length
Hind foot position inferred symmetric to front foot near rump (z=6,y=22) since hind legs are occluded by the long fur in this breed
notes: Guinea pigs lack an external tail, so no tail leaf was added (the 'rump' node is purely an internal spine joint for hind-leg attachment). Head counted as one leaf since it forms a distinct facial lobe even on a short neck. Ears/cheek fur are sub-flap detail per protocol and were not given leaves. Legs are rendered as single-segment stubs (attachment joint -> foot) rather than multi-joint chains because the heavy long-hair fur in this render occludes any visible knee/hock joints; this simplification is an inference, not a measured joint. Hind-foot position was inferred symmetric to the front foot (same relative offset from its spine node) since the fur hides the hind legs entirely in all three panels. Left/right assigned by animal's own orientation using the front (XY) view, with +x taken as the animal's right side.
